[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Euphame was recorded in Edinburgh in 1634. The FamilySearch index names her father as ''Johnne Glasgow'', while the structured family currently places her with [[Glassfuird-2|John Glassfuird, the Edinburgh slater]] and [[Morriel-1|Jonet Morriel]]. The original parish image is required before either household can be treated as proved.<ref name="ProjectSource1" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Current research ===

The structured father was verified on 15 October 2026 as Glassfuird-2. The earlier attachment to the minister Glassford-289 has already been corrected. This prose update preserves that correction; the original 1634 parish entry is still needed to resolve the surname conflict.


This is a genuine two-family conflation. FamilySearch X1Y9-V87 indexes Euphame in 1634 with father <code>Johnne Glasgow</code>. The same event is claimed in [[Glasgow-1030|Glasgow-1030]]'s biography as a child of John Glasgow and Jonet Mathie, while Euphame is structurally attached to [[Glassfuird-2|John Glassfuird, the Edinburgh slater]] and Jonet Morriel within an otherwise coherent Edinburgh Glassford sibling sequence.

The event's Edinburgh placement favours the Glassford household over the Glasgow High Kirk family, but the index surname favours Glasgow. The original parish image is required. It must not be attached to both families meanwhile.

The 1850-52 Euphemia Glasgow occurrence in the biography is more than two centuries later and unrelated.

This assessment draws on the cited records and public source material.<ref name="ProjectSource1">[https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTP4-XLG familysearch.org].</ref>

A possible identification concerns Eupham Glasgow and Alexander Hutcheson. The parish index records Eupham Glasgow with Alexander Hutcheson at Edinburgh on 8 December 1671.<ref>Scotland’s People, Old Parish Registers, banns and marriages, OPR 685 / 1/440 / 129, 1671-12-08, Edinburgh; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The index combines banns and marriage entries; the original register is required to establish the event type. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Effie Glasgow and Alexander Hutcshesone. The parish index records Effie Glasgow with Alexander Hutcshesone at Channelkirk on 17 September 1671.<ref>Scotland’s People, Old Parish Registers, banns and marriages, OPR 729/10 / 230, 1671-09-17, Channelkirk; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The index combines banns and marriage entries; the original register is required to establish the event type. The identification remains uncertain.
